actual_source_passages: 3.1 Define $\widetilde f(x)=c(f(x),h(x))$. If $\widetilde f(x)=\widetilde f(y)$, injectivity of the collar coordinates gives $f(x)=f(y)$ and $h(x)=h(y)$. By [F1], either $x=y$ or $x,y$ are the two preimages of one of the double arcs; the strict height inequality in step 2.1 excludes the latter. Thus $\widetilde f$ is injective. [given, F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 The map $f$ is an immersion, so its derivative is injective; adjoining the height coordinate preserves injectivity of the derivative, and the collar map $c$ is a local diffeomorphism. Hence $\widetilde f$ is an immersion. A continuous injection from compact $D^2$ to the Hausdorff space $B^4$ is a homeomorphism onto its image, so this injective immersion is a smooth embedding. Since $h^{-1}(0)=\partial D^2$, its preimage of $S^3=\partial B^4$ is exactly $\partial D^2$; the nonzero inward derivative established in step 2.1 gives the proper boundary collar condition in [F2]. The disk orientation transports through the embedding and its boundary remains the original oriented knot $K$. [given, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, construct] ∎

3.1 For $T=(C,D,f)$ define $T^*=(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb A}(C,\mathbb A)\{2\},\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R}(D,\mathbb R)\{2\},f^*)$, where $f^*$ is the transpose induced by a homotopy inverse $g$ to the reduced equivalence $f$. Finite freeness lets dualization commute with reduction and localization; it preserves chain homotopies and chain homotopy equivalences. Thus $T^*$ satisfies the LEO conditions, and dualizing both maps and the module-linear homotopy in a local-map square gives a local map in the reverse direction. The finite-free tensor-Hom isomorphisms identify $T\otimes T^*$ with $(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb A}(C,C)\{1\},\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R}(D,D)\{1\},F)$, where on reductions $F(\eta)=f\eta g$. The coevaluation maps from the unknot triple send $1$ to $\mathrm{id}_C$ and $\mathrm{id}_D$. The reduced square commutes up to the module-linear homotopy $H$ from $fg\simeq\mathrm{id}_D$, since $F(\mathrm{id}_C)=fg$. After inverting $h$, the BN coevaluation map $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R[h^{-1}]}(D[h^{-1}],D[h^{-1}])$ sends $1$ to $\mathrm{id}_D$; under a chosen homotopy equivalence $D[h^{-1}]\simeq\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$ it is homotopic to the identity map of the rank-one endomorphism complex, so it is a homotopy equivalence by [F2]. The reverse evaluation maps are the graded evaluations $\phi\otimes c\mapsto\phi(c)$ on the finite-free tensor-Hom identifications, with the standard Hom differential $d\phi=-(-1)^{|\phi|}\phi d$. They are chain maps because the two terms in $d(\phi\otimes c)$ evaluate to $-(-1)^{|\phi|}\phi(dc)$ and $+(-1)^{|\phi|}\phi(dc)$. Their reduced square commutes up to the homotopy $\phi\otimes c\mapsto\phi(H(c))$, and after localization evaluation identifies with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R[h^{-1}]}(\mathbb R[h^{-1}],\mathbb R[h^{-1}])\to\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$, an isomorphism. Hence the two evaluation maps are local maps in both directions, proving $T\otimes T^*$ locally equivalent to the unknot triple and $T^*$ is an inverse. Finite tensor-Hom associativity, the graded flip, and the unknot's identity endomorphism give associativity, commutativity and the unit, so local-equivalence classes form an abelian group. [F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra, construct]
